blocks.text: Buying Vacant Land or a Building Lot in Maple Ridge, BC

parts.t: Vacant land in Maple Ridge falls into three distinct categories: serviced urban residential infill lots inside the Urban Area Boundary (such as Silver Valley, Albion, West Central, and East Central), rural 1-to-5-acre building parcels in Websters Corners, Thornhill, and Whonnock, and multi-family or commercial development sites along the Lougheed Transit Corridor and Town Centre.

Before making an offer on any vacant lot in Maple Ridge, buyers must confirm whether municipal water, sanitary sewer, and storm sewer connections are at the lot line—or whether the site requires a private drilled well, an engineered Type 1/2/3 septic field, rock blasting, or road dedication.

blocks.text: Development Permit Areas, Thornhill Urban Reserve & Servicing Checks

parts.t: The City of Maple Ridge Official Community Plan (OCP) enforces strict Development Permit Areas (DPAs) for watercourse protection (riparian setbacks along Kanaka Creek, Alouette River, and Whonnock Creek), steep-slope geotechnical hazards (common in Silver Valley and Grant Hill), and wildfire interface zones. In addition, parcels inside the 343-hectare Thornhill Urban Reserve cannot be subdivided below 2.0 hectares (4.9 acres) until city population exceeds 100,000 and an area plan is adopted.

parts.t: Where are serviced building lots available in Maple Ridge?

What are the minimum lot sizes for rural land in Maple Ridge?

Under Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, RS-2 Single Detached Suburban Residential requires at least 0.4 ha (1 acre), RS-3 Single Detached Rural Residential requires 0.8 ha (2 acres) with community water or 2.0 ha (4.9 acres) without, and A-1 Agricultural requires 2.0 ha (4.9 acres).
Can I subdivide land inside the Thornhill Urban Reserve right now?

Under Maple Ridge Official Community Plan Section 10.2.2, subdivision inside the 343-hectare Thornhill Urban Reserve below a 2.0-hectare (4.9-acre) minimum is held until Maple Ridge's population exceeds 100,000 and a comprehensive area plan and servicing strategy are adopted.
Does GST apply to vacant lots and land in Maple Ridge?

Most vacant land sales—including new subdivision lots and commercial or development land—are subject to 5% federal GST, though select personal-use resales by an individual who never subdivided or used the land in a business may be exempt; always confirm GST status in the contract.
How much down payment do lenders require on vacant land in BC?

Canadian banks and credit unions typically require a 35% to 50% down payment for raw or unserviced rural land, and 25% to 35% for a fully serviced urban residential lot, unless the purchase is bundled with a residential construction draw mortgage.
What are watercourse and slope Development Permit Areas (DPAs)?

In Maple Ridge, creeks and ravines carry 15-to-30-metre Riparian Areas Protection Regulation (RAPR) setbacks, and hillside lots in Silver Valley or Thornhill require geotechnical engineering reports before a building permit can be issued.
